en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its nearly perfect conical shape.
The Cagayan River, flowing through the provinces of Cagayan and Isabela, is the longest river in the Philippines.
Taal Volcano is uniquely situated on Volcano Island, which is entirely surrounded by Lake Taal in Batangas province.
The critically endangered Philippine eagle primarily inhabits the tropical rainforests found on the island of Mindanao.
Mount Apo, located in the Davao region, is the highest and most prominent mountain in the Philippines.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is a protected marine sanctuary located in the middle of the Sulu Sea.
The amihan is the cool northeast monsoon wind that brings dry weather to the Philippines from November to April.
Abaca, a plant native to the Philippines, is harvested for its exceptionally strong fibers used in making ropes.
The Sibuyan Sea is a distinct body of water that separates the large island of Luzon from the Visayas.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features a navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
The Rafflesia, a parasitic plant found in Luzon and Mindanao, produces the largest individual flower on Earth.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao province were carved into the mountains by indigenous people over two thousand years ago.
